page: Google Cloud Platform x4-megamem-960-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 960 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16384 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of approximately 17.07 GB per execution thread. The bare-metal design grants direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, targeting workloads requiring extensive single-system resource aggregation. Local disk storage is not bundled with the server, necessitating external or network-attached persistent storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent data. Additionally, the configuration includes no discrete GPUs or hardware acceleration modules.

The instance architecture delivers substantial multi-threaded parallelism across its 960 dedicated cores alongside 16 terabytes of addressable volatile memory. This setup enables large-scale operations to function entirely in system memory, avoiding disk paging or inter-node cluster latency. The absence of virtualization layers ensures consistent execution timing and memory throughput across all processor sockets.

From a cost and operational perspective, deploying a bare-metal server of this magnitude concentrates capital into dedicated hardware capacity. Efficient utilization requires consistent memory saturation and multi-core thread engagement, as unused capacity on a 16-terabyte platform represents substantial overhead. A notable structural tradeoff is the reliance on external storage architectures, which places overall I/O performance on the attached network storage fabric rather than on-bus local NVMe drives.

Google Cloud Platform x4-megamem-960-metal is engineered primarily for extreme-scale enterprise data workloads. Common target deployments include ultra-large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive transactional processing systems, memory-bound enterprise resource planning engines, and consolidated real-time analytical platforms holding multi-terabyte data tables entirely in memory.
